items.topic: Arbitrary deletions and absent BLO visits
items.headline: How booth-level officers in Bihar are deleting voters arbitrarily
items.what_is_reported: Scroll reported that 200 booths across 58 constituencies in Bihar recorded between 324 and 641 deletions each in the draft roll, and that most deleted voters it met in 10 of those booths had been marked absent or shifted though they had lived at their addresses for years. It reported that interviews with 17 BLOs showed no consistent procedure for deletions.
items.quote: Most voters we met had been marked either “absent,” or “shifted,” even though they had been residing at their addresses for many years. Several claimed that their BLOs didn’t even visit their homes even though the poll panel categorically stated that the special intensive revision would involve “house-to-house verification”.
items.figures: 200 booths, 58 constituencies, 26 districts; 324 to 641 deletions per booth; 77,454 deleted across the 200 booths; 100 people interviewed; 17 BLOs interviewed
items.official_response: Parth Gupta, the electoral registration officer for Purnia, acknowledged that one deleted voter, Jhurana Das, should not have been asked to furnish her parents' documents: “Please provide her details and I will look into it.”

items.topic: Arbitrary deletions and absent BLO visits
items.headline: ‘I didn’t know my name was deleted’: Voters in Okhla on the pre-SIR ‘clean-up’
items.what_is_reported: Newslaundry reported that several Okhla voters deleted from the Delhi roll before the SIR began said they received no notice or hearing and learnt of it only when they tried to take part in the SIR. It reported that 34,644 names were deleted in Okhla during the 2026 mapping phase against 9,170 in all of 2025.
items.quote: In Okhla alone, 9,170 names were deleted in 2025. But in 2026, during the mapping phase, a further 34,644 additional names were deleted – nearly 4 times as many in roughly half the time.
items.figures: about 1.55 crore voters last year, about 1.45 crore when SIR began; more than 47 lakh excluded from the draft of August 31; about 33 lakh notices; more than 10 lakh net deletions before SIR
items.official_response: Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar said that no voter had been deleted without an inquiry and an opportunity for a hearing.

items.topic: Booth level officers' deaths and workload
items.headline: Two suicides, BLO protests threaten to disrupt SIR in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Rajasthan
items.what_is_reported: The Indian Express reported the deaths of two BLOs, Aneesh George in Kannur, Kerala, whose family alleged he was under pressure to finish by December 4, and Mukesh Jangid in Jaipur, whose suicide note, according to police, said his supervisor threatened suspension if he missed his target. It reported a statewide boycott of SIR work announced by revenue employees in Tamil Nadu over workload.
items.quote: “A suicide note was recovered from his body which stated that he was facing extreme work pressure from his supervisor. He was asked to complete his target of the SIR process or he will be suspended. He stated in the note that he wasn’t able to sleep at night for the last few days.”
items.figures: 1,065 enumeration forms issued to George, 50 left to distribute on November 16
items.official_response: Kannur District Collector Arun K Vijayan's report indicated that the BLO was not under any work pressure. The newspaper's calls to Rajasthan CEO Naveen were not answered.

items.topic: Booth level officers' deaths and workload
items.headline: 4 deaths in a week: 2 woman assistant BLOs die of ‘heart attack’ in Gujarat amid concerns on ‘SIR work pressure’
items.what_is_reported: The Indian Express reported that two women assistant BLOs died of heart attacks in Tapi and Vadodara, bringing BLO deaths in Gujarat that week to four. The husband of one said she was a heart patient who had asked to be excused from BLO duty.
items.quote: With the two cases, the number of deaths of BLOs in Gujarat this week rose to four. A BLO from Kheda reportedly died of heart attack on Thursday and another BLO allegedly died by suicide in Gir Somnath district on Friday.
items.figures: four deaths in a week in Gujarat
items.official_response: Vadodara District Collector Anil Dhameliya said that no formal request was made to excuse her, and "there is no excessive workload on the BLOs". An unnamed official: "With a large workforce of over two lakh involved in the SIR work, these deaths can be termed as natural. Linking these to SIR is not justified and logical."

items.topic: Booth level officers' deaths and workload
items.headline: Little sleep, no pay: India's poll workers flag harsh conditions amid uproar over deaths
items.what_is_reported: The BBC reported that ten BLOs it spoke to in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal said they worked 14 to 15 hours a day with little rest, and that families linked more than a dozen deaths of poll workers, by alleged suicide or heart attack, to election work stress. The BBC said it had not independently verified the causes of death. It also reported BLOs saying the SIR app crashed often and that many had not received payment.
items.quote: They said they were working 14–15 hours a day with little rest, minimal sleep, and meagre pay. The punishing schedules have sparked outrage, especially after more than a dozen workers, including Kumar, died. Families have linked the deaths - from alleged suicides or heart attacks - to election work-related stress. The BBC has not independently verified the causes of death.
items.figures: 10 BLOs interviewed; 14-15 hours a day; more than a dozen workers died; BLO pay doubled from 6,000 to 12,000 rupees
items.official_response: The EC has not responded to a detailed list of questions from the BBC. Media reports quoting a court affidavit say the EC has denied opposition claims linking BLO deaths to SIR work, calling them "false, exaggerated and politically motivated".

items.headline: Form-7 misuse: Supreme Court to consider Congress MP’s plea alleging targeted deletions in U.P.
items.what_is_reported: The Hindu reported that the Supreme Court agreed to consider an application by Congress MP Tanuj Punia, who alleged that Form 7 objections in the Uttar Pradesh SIR were filed with false particulars, forged signatures and in the names of people who later denied filing them. The application cited one person filing objections against 32 electors in Hata, Kushinagar.
items.quote: Mr. Punia’s application said there were credible reports indicating that “numerous” Form-7 applications were generated and submitted with incomplete or false particulars of the objector, invalid identifying details, forged signatures, and, in several instances, in the names of persons who had subsequently denied filing any such objections.
items.figures: 32 electors objected to by one person in Hata; 700-800 Form 7 objections in four booths of Khalilabad, as claimed by the UP Congress president

items.headline: Uttarakhand SIR: Who is targeting Muslim voters?
items.what_is_reported: Newslaundry reported from an investigation in Uttarakhand that numerous applications were filed to remove Muslim voters from the rolls, and that some people named as objectors later submitted affidavits stating they had never filed them and that their names, EPIC numbers and signatures had been used without their consent.
items.quote: Some of the individuals in whose names these objections were filed later submitted affidavits stating that they had never filed them in the first place. They alleged that their names, EPIC numbers, and signatures had been fraudulently used.

items.headline: Civil society groups, Congress demand FIRs over bulk Form 7s seeking deletion of names
items.what_is_reported: The Hindu reported that as of September 28, 4,000 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names had been filed in Karnataka, and that ten people filed Form 7s seeking deletion of 1,363 names in Babaleshwar in one day. It reported that in many cases the voters' details were already printed on the forms with only the objector's name handwritten. Civil society groups and the Karnataka Congress, who alleged the forms largely target Muslim voters, demanded that the Commission lodge criminal complaints.
items.quote: As of September 28, 4,000 Form-7 applications were filed in the State, mostly targeting Muslim voters in constituencies represented by both Congress and BJP. ... Ten people filed Form-7s seeking deletion of 1,363 names in Babaleshwar in just one day. In many cases, the Form-7s submitted had details of the voters “already printed”, with only the objector’s name handwritten.
items.figures: 4,000 Form-7 applications as of September 28; 1,363 names in Babaleshwar by ten people in one day; in Bhalki 30 people filed Form-7s seeking deletion of 1,700 names

items.headline: Karnataka SIR: ECI flags bulk Form 7 claims, orders action against false declarations
items.what_is_reported: The New Indian Express reported that the Commission wrote to election officials in Bengaluru that instances of bulk Form 7 applications had come to its notice, with allegations that some were not genuine, and directed Electoral Registration Officers to act against applicants who knowingly make false declarations, after an inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.
items.quote: The Commission said, “Instances of bulk Form 7 applications had come to its notice and that allegations had been made that some of these applications were not genuine. It is directed the concerned EROs to initiate action against applicants who knowingly make false statements or declarations in writing while submitting Forms 6, 6A, 7 or 8.”
items.official_response: The report is itself of a Commission letter, quoted above.

items.topic: Changes to Form 6 without Gazette amendment
items.headline: Express Special | EC changes Form 6 for new voters without amendment to rules; seeks SIR details of parents
items.what_is_reported: The Indian Express reported that the online Form 6 on the Commission's ECINET portal carried a new declaration asking whether the applicant or their parents or grandparents were in the electoral roll of the last SIR, although the statutory form had not been amended. It reported that the section was not marked mandatory but the user could not proceed to submission without completing it, and that the downloadable Form 6 on the same portal did not include it.
items.quote: For the first time, the Election Commission’s online version of the electors’ registration form, known as Form 6, has a new section that seeks the status of the applicant’s parents vis-a vis the last Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, even though the statutory form itself has not been amended, The Indian Express has learnt. ... While the new part has not been marked mandatory, the user cannot move forward toward the submission before completing it.
items.figures: over 5.58 crore names deleted in 10 states and three UTs; visible for all states and UTs where SIR concluded in 2025-2026 or is ongoing, except Bihar and Assam
items.official_response: The EC did not respond to a request for comment and Legislative Department Secretary Rajiv Mani could not be reached despite repeated attempts.

items.topic: Changes to Form 6 without Gazette amendment
items.headline: ‘Illegal, unauthorised’: Election Commissioners objected to Form 6 change
items.what_is_reported: The Indian Express reported that on May 16 Commissioner Vivek Joshi recorded that Form 6 is prescribed by statute and cannot be altered without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that Commissioner Sandhu concurred on May 19. It reported that the declaration was added to the online form anyway, and that on August 13 Sandhu wrote that the changes were unauthorised and must be removed immediately.
items.quote: “In spite of these very clear views expressed by two Election Commissioners,” Sandhu wrote, the “unauthorised/ illegal changes in Form-6 on the portal” had not been removed and the original form had not been restored. The changes “must be removed immediately so that young and would-be first time voters, who are otherwise eligible, can register themselves as voters as per law, without any harassment”, he wrote.
items.figures: Joshi note May 16; Sandhu concurred May 19; first reported July 12; Sandhu note August 13

items.topic: Changes to Form 6 without Gazette amendment
items.headline: EC removes Form 6 change two Commissioners had called ‘illegal’
items.what_is_reported: The Indian Express reported that on the night of 29 to 30 September 2026 the Commission removed the SIR declaration from the online Form 6 on ECINET for states where the SIR has concluded. It reported that the declaration was still there for states where the SIR is still ongoing.
items.quote: On Wednesday night, the ECINET portal no longer showed the declaration – which had been inserted in between Sections J and K of the Form 6 online – for the states where the final SIR electoral rolls have been published so far. The declaration was still there for those states where the SIR is still ongoing.
items.official_response: The article cites the Commission's September 26 announcement that ‘for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used’.

items.topic: Deaths linked by families to hearings
items.headline: Elderly man dies due to cardiac arrest during SIR hearing, kin allege ‘excessive stress’
items.what_is_reported: The Indian Express reported that Kanchan Kumar Mondal, 75, died of cardiac arrest while waiting in a queue for an SIR hearing at the Rampurhat-1 block office in Birbhum, and that his family alleged the SIR process had caused him excessive stress. It reported a similar death of Madan Ghosh at a hearing in Howrah the previous day.
items.quote: He was waiting in a long queue in front of the BDO office when he suddenly fell ill. ... According to hospital sources, Mondal died due to cardiac arrest. However, his wife and family alleged that he had fallen ill due to excessive stress related to the SIR process, and they held the Election Commission responsible for his death.
items.figures: aged 75

items.topic: Deaths linked by families to hearings
items.headline: FIR against ECI in West Bengal over alleged suicide of elderly man due to SIR 'anxiety'
items.what_is_reported: The New Indian Express, citing PTI, reported that police in Purulia registered an FIR, naming no official, on a complaint by the son of Durjan Majhi, 82, who died allegedly by suicide on 29 December hours before he was due at an SIR hearing. The family alleged he acted out of anxiety over the SIR.
items.quote: "The case includes charges of abetment of suicide and criminal conspiracy against officials of the Election Commission. No official was named in the FIR," an officer was quoted as saying by the news agency.
items.figures: aged 82; Trinamool Congress claimed at least 40 deaths since November 2025

items.topic: Documents: women after marriage, migrants, Aadhaar
items.headline: Bihar booth officials accept voter forms without documents, using discretion
items.what_is_reported: India Today reported from Hajipur and Muzaffarpur that BLOs were accepting and submitting enumeration forms without supporting documents at their own discretion, and that BLOs admitted the practice differed by place, with some accepting Aadhaar and others not.
items.quote: BLOs admitted that discretion is being exercised differently across locations. Some accept Aadhaar, others do not.

items.topic: Documents: women after marriage, migrants, Aadhaar
items.headline: Married women facing the heat of SIR in Bihar
items.what_is_reported: The Hindu reported that married women in Bihar born after 1 July 1987 faced difficulty because they needed documents from their parental homes rather than their marital homes. It quoted women in Araria, Katihar and Saharsa districts who said their parents had no documents to give.
items.quote: Married women born between July 1, 1987 to December 2, 2004 and born after December 2, 2004 are at the receiving end in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) as they need to provide the documents related to the maternal house (Maika) instead of in-laws (Sasural).

items.topic: Documents: women after marriage, migrants, Aadhaar
items.headline: Pay loss, travel woes to reach SIR hearings; migrants forced to leave to ensure electoral enrollment
items.what_is_reported: The Telegraph reported that migrant workers from Murshidabad were served hearing notices two to three days before their hearings and had to travel home from Uttar Pradesh and Kerala without reserved seats. One worker was summoned because his name appeared in the 2002 roll without a surname, and another arrived after the day's hearings had ended. It reported that, as of its publication, the Commission had issued no directive allowing online hearings for those outside the state.
items.quote: However, with notices in many cases being served barely 48 hours before the scheduled hearing, migrant workers find themselves scrambling to return home in time, often without seats and at a high financial cost.
items.figures: about 1,400 km from Meerut; nearly 2,600 km from Kollam; a loss of about Rs 15,000 for one worker
items.official_response: Samserganj BDO Sujit Kumar Lodh: “After receiving the notice, those who are unable to attend the hearing within the stipulated period because of being out of the house can submit a written application citing specific reasons, and a second hearing date will be scheduled for them later.”

items.headline: New voters list in Indian state includes wrong photos and dead people
items.what_is_reported: The BBC reported that voters in villages near Patna told it the Bihar draft roll carried wrong photographs, duplicate entries and the name of a person who died more than five years earlier. It reported that in Danara village many residents were not sure officials had visited their homes.
items.quote: He shared pages showing his family's details - pointing out errors, including the wrong photo next to his name. "I have no idea whose photo it is," he says ... He points out the name of a cousin who died more than five years back but still figures on the list - and at least two names that appear twice.
items.figures: 72.4 million names on the draft roll, 6.5 million fewer than before
items.official_response: In response to the BBC's questions, the Election Commission shared its 24 June order on conducting the SIR and a 27 July press note ... "Further, [the commission] does not take any responsibility of any other misinformation or unsubstantiated allegations being floated around by some vested interests," it added in the response.

items.topic: ECINet and access of electoral registration officers
items.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity
items.what_is_reported: The Indian Express reported that Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi recorded in notes from November 2025 to August 2026 that control of the roll software was being centralised in the Commission's IT division. It reported that on August 14 Sandhu wrote that many Chief Electoral Officers, District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers had told him they lacked proper and complete access to ERONet, and that on July 29 both Commissioners wrote separately to the Cabinet Secretary about a change in work allocation.
items.quote: But many had told him they did not have “proper and complete access” to ERONet and were therefore unable to perform their statutory duties properly. Their powers, he said, had been “curtailed by centralised control of ERONet at DG(IT) level”.
items.figures: notes dated November 4, 2025; January 2, 2026; April 16; May 29; July 13; July 28-30; August 14
items.official_response: The Election Commission and the two ECs, Sandhu and Joshi, did not respond to calls and questionnaires emailed by The Indian Express seeking comment.

items.topic: ECINet and access of electoral registration officers
items.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out: EC’s flawed system
items.what_is_reported: The Indian Express reported that Goa's Electoral Registration Officers heard electors flagged for logical discrepancies and found 97 of them eligible, but could not reverse the earlier decisions on ECINet because the permission was controlled from Delhi. It reported that the Goa Chief Electoral Officer's office wrote eight times in seven days asking for a rollback option, and that all 97 were missing from the final roll published on February 21.
items.quote: On February 21, the final roll was published. The Indian Express checked all 97 names against it. Until September 20, all 97 are still missing.
items.figures: 649 electors came forward with documents or objections; 97 found eligible; eight emails in seven days (February 11 to 17)
items.official_response: Goa Chief Electoral Officer Sanjay Goel: “We apprised the ECI about the cases to be included wherein voters were flagged for logical discrepancies.” ... “The call (to not include) was theirs. But there has to be some mechanism (in ECINET) to re-include voters at the ERO level.” The DG IT did not respond to a questionnaire. The Indian Express reported on 2026-09-27 that, in the note issued after the Commission's meeting of September 26, the Commission says 81 of the 97 have now filled Form 6 and the CEO has been directed to facilitate their inclusion (https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/election-commission-nine-new-decisions-what-changes-and-what-doesnt-10895475/).

items.headline: SIR: Not even 0.5% submit enumeration forms online amid website glitches
items.what_is_reported: The Hindu reported that 13 days into the Karnataka SIR only 0.41% of enumeration forms had been submitted online, and that voters complained of captcha failures, server errors and an ECINet search that failed to find records appearing in the published rolls. It reported that online submission required a mobile number linked to the voter's EPIC.
items.quote: Voters have complained of continuous glitches and server issues on the ECINet portal, making the online process difficult. As of 6 p.m. on Sunday, only 0.41% of the forms were submitted online.
items.figures: 0.41% submitted online; up 0.23% between July 5 and July 12
items.official_response: Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar said the process was still under way. However, the CEO did not comment on the technical glitches reported by voters.

items.headline: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps
items.what_is_reported: The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi formally objected on record at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders that, they said, were taken without their knowledge. The objections concerned new voter registration, deletion and restoration of voters, appeals against orders restoring voters, and the custody and security of the electoral roll. The newspaper said it had seen each of these exchanges.
items.quote: But Sandhu and Joshi have formally objected, on record, at least 14 times over the last 10 months – four times on a single day – to decisions taken and orders issued, they say, without their knowledge. ... For, the objections relate to the core of the Election Commission’s mandate: new voter registration, deletion and restoration of voters in the rolls; filing of appeals against orders restoring voters in the SIR process; and the custody, and security, of the entire electoral roll itself.
items.figures: at least 14 times over the last 10 months; four times on a single day; more than 13 crore names struck off the draft rolls in 30 States and Union Territories
items.official_response: The Indian Express wrote that it sent a questionnaire to the Commission on September 21 and emailed both Commissioners, and "There was no response." The Commission's later statement, as reported by The Hindu on 2026-09-23: "All decisions of the Election Commission of India, including SIR [the ongoing special intensive revision of electoral rolls], have been unanimous and with the approval of both the Election Commissioners and the Chief Election Commissioner."

items.headline: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps
items.what_is_reported: The Indian Express reported that in August Commissioner Sandhu wrote to Commission officials asking who had authorised and who had filed appeals on behalf of the Commission against voters whom judicial officers had included in West Bengal. It reported that he recorded that neither he, nor Joshi, nor the Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal had been informed of the basis or process of filing those appeals.
items.quote: In August, he wrote to Commission officials asking, “Who was authorised to file these appeals on behalf of ECI, and by whom?” and “Who actually filed these appeals on behalf of ECI?” He recorded that neither he nor Joshi nor the current Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal had been informed about the basis or process of filing the appeals.
items.figures: 38 lakh appeals pending before the tribunals: 22.21 lakh filed by deleted voters seeking to be restored; 16.10 lakh filed against voters the judicial officers had included

items.headline: Declared Dead in Draft Electoral Roll, Bihar Voter Appears in Supreme Court
items.what_is_reported: The Wire reported that Mintu Paswan of Ara, Bhojpur, who was declared dead in the Bihar draft roll, appeared alive in the Supreme Court on 12 August 2025, produced by petitioner Yogendra Yadav. Paswan told The Wire he had filled the enumeration form and that the BLO came to his house only after he complained.
items.quote: Forty-one-year-old Mintu Paswan, a resident of Bihar’s Ara assembly constituency in Bhojpur district was declared dead by the Election Commission in its ongoing 'special intensive revision' of the electoral rolls in the poll-bound state. But on August 12, Paswan appeared in the Supreme Court, demonstrably alive.
items.figures: 65 lakh left out of the draft roll of August 1; 22 lakh declared deceased
items.official_response: Senior advocate Rakesh Dwivedi, for the Commission, called the production of Paswan "drama". The bench said there may have been an "inadvertent error", which could be rectified.

items.headline: How ECI’s dubious software branded 3.66 crore voters in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh as suspects
items.what_is_reported: The Reporters' Collective reported, from internal records it acquired, that the Commission's software initially flagged 1.31 crore voters in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh for logical discrepancies, and that officials had no written instructions on how to resolve them. It reported that no criteria for summoning voters had been made public.
items.quote: The untested software deployed by the Election Commission of India (ECI) without written instructions, protocols and manuals, red-flagged 1.31 crore voters in West Bengal and 2.35 crore voters in Madhya Pradesh as suspicious, putting their voting rights in jeopardy.
items.figures: 1.31 crore (17.11%) in West Bengal; 2.35 crore (nearly 40%) in Madhya Pradesh; West Bengal count fell to 95 lakh by January 2; 24 lakh of 95 lakh to receive notices
items.official_response: We asked ECI about the criterion used, but they did not reply at the time of filing the report.

items.headline: ECI misled the Supreme Court on SIR in West Bengal
items.what_is_reported: The Reporters' Collective reported that hearing notices in West Bengal were generated in bulk by the Commission's software for logical discrepancies, and that EROs it interviewed were signing 4,000 to 5,000 printed notices each day. It reported that the software transliterated names from Bengali into English before matching, so that differing spellings, such as Xalxo and Khalkho, triggered a discrepancy. This contrasts with the Commission's submission to the Supreme Court that there was no automated generation of notices.
items.quote: We spoke to two EROs, one in Kolkata and one in Nadia, who, along with a few deputies, were signing 4,000 to 5,000 printed hearing notices each day. ... In numerous instances, the traditional English spelling of a surname differs from the software's automated transliteration of the Bengali script.
items.figures: over 1.5 crore summons prepared; 95.39 lakh delivered and 30 lakh attended by January 24; software marked more than 1.31 crore voters; over 32 lakh unmapped in the draft of December 16
items.official_response: We sent questions to the ECI to respond to the story. It had not responded by the time of publication. The Commission's submission to the Court, as quoted: “There is no automated generation of notices…. EROs (Electoral Registration Officers) are signing them off after application of mind.”

items.headline: The many categories of SIR’s logical discrepancy list keep voters on toes
items.what_is_reported: The Hindu reported that up to 11 categories of logical discrepancy were being applied in the third phase, up from four in West Bengal, including a sibling age gap of nine months or less, which flagged a Delhi resident's twin children, and a marital mapping mismatch where a woman is linked to her father in the old roll and her husband in the new. It reported that the term has never been clearly defined in any official communication.
items.quote: The problem in this is that “logical discrepancies” has never been clearly defined in any official communication — neither in the Election Commission’s notice in May 2026 nor in the original SIR order from June 2025.
items.figures: about 1.36 crore notices in West Bengal; 19.33 lakh in Delhi; 20.35 lakh in Karnataka; up to 11 categories against original four

items.headline: ECI Skipped its Fraud-Busting Software, Flooding Bihar Voter Roll with Lakhs of Suspect Duplicates
items.what_is_reported: The Reporters' Collective reported that a top Commission official and four Bihar EROs confirmed the Commission did not run its de-duplication software during the Bihar SIR, and did not give state officials access to it. It quoted the official saying the focus was on document collection. Its own analysis of the final roll found 14.35 lakh suspect duplicate entries.
items.quote: A top official at ECI who spoke with us said, “We did not touch deduplication during SIR. Mostly our focus was on document collection.”
items.figures: 14.35 lakh suspect duplicate entries in the final roll, 3.4 lakh exact matches on name, relative's name and age; 5.56 lakh suspect duplicates in the draft in 142 constituencies
items.official_response: We emailed questions to the ECI and its top official in Bihar, the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO). Neither of them replied to us.

items.headline: A Centralised Batch System Challenged Bengal Voters Who Were Cleared by Judicial Officers, Records Show
items.what_is_reported: The Wire reported that tribunal orders in Murshidabad record the Additional Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal as the appellant against electors whom judicial officers had restored to the roll. It reported that appeal records it reviewed carry identical, minute-level timestamps across different constituencies, for example at least six appeals at 19:04 on 8 April 2026, which it reads as indicating a centralised script rather than individual filings. It also reported a December 2025 letter from the WBCS (Executive) Officers' Association complaining of system-driven deletions that bypassed EROs.
items.quote: The second line of the order reads, "This is an appeal filed by the Additional CEO as regards" the elector, who is then named in full. ... Screenshots from the Election Commission’s appeal portal reviewed by The Wire show at least six such appeals carrying the exact timestamp 08/04/2026 | 19:04.
items.figures: 38,31,429 appeals filed; 22,21,118 from excluded voters; 16,10,311 against inclusion; 32,77,360 electors cleared by judicial officers
items.official_response: The ECI has not yet clarified why more than 16 lakh challenges were filed by the commission, how the electors were selected and what explains the batch pattern visible in the appeal records.

items.headline: SIR summit: A 145-year climb for Bengal tribunal judge swamped with 5 lakh cases
items.what_is_reported: The Telegraph reported that Justice (retd) Indrajit Chatterjee, who presides over one of the 19 SIR appellate tribunals and hears appeals from 11 Murshidabad constituencies, has written to the Chief Justice of Calcutta High Court that he wants to resign, citing a long commute. He told the newspaper he can decide about 10 appeals a day, has decided 425, restoring 350, while around 5.3 lakh are pending before him. It also reported that two other tribunal judges had resigned earlier, citing personal reasons.
items.quote: “I have decided 425 appeals so far. The names of 350 appellants have been restored to the rolls and 75 have been struck off,” Justice Chatterjee told The Telegraph on Wednesday.
items.figures: Appeals disposed of: 425; appeals pending: around 5.3 lakh; about 10 appeals a day; around 145 years at that rate; 82.35 per cent genuine voters; over 38 lakh appeals filed, over 37 lakh pending, about 1.02 lakh disposed of (per the Commission's affidavit)
items.official_response: An official of the state election commission: “The tribunals were set up on the Supreme Court’s order. A panel headed by the chief justice of Calcutta High Court takes decisions regarding the functioning of the appellate tribunals. We cannot interfere.”

items.headline: Final verification for 46.63L flagged voters launched
items.what_is_reported: The Hans India reported that Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer announced a door-to-door re-check of the 46,62,583 names deleted so far, before the final roll of 16 October. Booth officers carry polling-station lists and help anyone deleted in error to file Form 6.
items.quote: Chief Electoral Officer and E O Vivek Yadav said Booth Level Officers (BLOs) would begin fresh door-to-door verification from Thursday, carrying polling-station-wise lists of 46,62,583 deleted names.
items.figures: 46,62,583 names on the lists; 44,89,512 electors not available at their registered addresses at enumeration; 1,73,071 found ineligible as on 6 October; draft roll of 31 July 3,71,38,182 electors

not_read.headline: EC desperate to reduce logical discrepancy hearings
